title: Current Practice and Further Development of Cardiac Rehabilitation in Patients with Heart Failure: An Observational Study
summary: For people with heart failure, there are currently no uniform treatment standards in cardiac rehabilitation, meaning that treatment varies from clinic to clinic. In order to enable comparable rehabilitation services, this study investigates how patients with heart failure are currently cared for in cardiac rehabilitation. The study examines which rehabilitation therapies patients receive, how their health develops during and after rehabilitation, and where there is potential to improve rehabilitation and follow-up care. It also analyzes whether there are differences between subgroups (e.g., gender, type of rehabilitation). Questionnaires and interviews at different measurement points will be used to collect data. The results will contribute to the development of specific recommendations for uniform and needs-based rehabilitation for heart failure patients.

interventions.name: Patients undergoing cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure are surveyed using written questionnaires at three points in time (start of rehabilitation, end of rehabilitation, 6-month follow-up) and qualitative interviews at two points in time (end of rehabilitation, 6-month follow-up). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Rehabilitation patients of working age undergoing rehabilitation after hospital stay or medical rehabilitation who have heart failure with reduced pumping function (HFrEF; EF < 50%) or preserved pumping function (HFpEF; EF ≥ 50%)
Exclusion criteria:
NYHA class IV rehabilitation patients (persistent symptoms, even at rest), individuals with insufficient language skills, or those who do not consent to participate in the study
